goldens.comment: In GroupPermissionsV2.canManage(), the permission fallback checks for both VIEW and MANAGE scopes (hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)), but canManage() should only grant access for MANAGE scope, not VIEW. This means users with only VIEW permission on groups can pass the canManage() check, granting them write access they should not have. The canView() method correctly checks both VIEW and MANAGE, but canManage() should only check MANAGE.
goldens.reasoning: C1 points out that canManage() checks for both VIEW and MANAGE, so a user with only VIEW gets manage access. That is the same issue as G1.

goldens.comment: In getGroupIdsWithViewPermission, hasPermission is called with groupResource.getId() and the same groupResource.getId() is added to granted, but hasPermission resolves resources by name (treating the argument as a group id) and the GroupPermissionEvaluator contract says this method returns group IDs that are later used as UserModel.GROUPS and in getUsersCount group filters. This mismatch means per-group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permissions may not yield the expected group IDs for filtering and counts, and evaluation may effectively only look at the type-level 'all-groups' resource; consider revisiting whether this should operate on the underlying group ids (resource names) instead so it aligns with the JPA queries and the interface contract.
goldens.reasoning: C2 notes that getGroupIdsWithViewPermission uses the resource's internal ID instead of the group ID, which should come from the resource name. That is the same mismatch G2 describes.

candidates: Privilege escalation in GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() no-arg method: calls hasPermission with both VIEW and MANAGE scopes, granting manage access to principals holding only VIEW scope. Should only check for MANAGE scope like the per-group canManage(GroupModel) overload does.

Resource internal ID vs group domain ID mismatch in GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission(): groupResource.getId() returns the authorization resource's internal primary key instead of the actual group ID. Should use groupResource.getName() since group resources are created with the group's domain ID as the resource name.

Per-user canView filter removed from UsersResource.searchForUser and BruteForceUsersResource.searchForUser: the old code applied .filter(usersEvaluator::canView) to individual user results for fine-grained V1 per-user permission checks. The new code only uses group-based filtering, potentially exposing users that should be hidden under V1 fine-grained authorization for users with partial view permissions granted via V1 user-specific policies.
